The problem was in the entries.

03 / System boundary

Everything runs on the device.

One Flutter process, a local asset bundle, and an in-memory search index. Dictionary updates travel with a new application build.

Android

Kotlin activity, Gradle, Java 17. Application ID: com.nur.arabicmyanmardictionary. SDK values come from Flutter.

iOS

Swift app and scene delegates. Same bundle ID. The Xcode deployment target is iOS 13.0; building requires macOS and Xcode.

Linux

C++ GTK runner and CMake. Initial window: 1280 × 720. Distribution includes the executable, native libraries and asset data.

05 / Search pipeline

Normalized matching.
Original text for reading.

Three normalized fields per record are cached: plain Arabic, vocalized Arabic and Myanmar. The result list returns original entry objects, so search normalization never removes vowel marks from the display.

Normalization

Lowercase; remove harakat and tatweel; fold alef variants to ا, ى to ي, ؤ to و, and ئ to ي; collapse whitespace. Myanmar script characters remain unchanged.

No stemming, root analysis, transliteration, fuzzy matching or Zawgyi input conversion.

Ranking

  1. Exact field match
  2. Field prefix
  3. Word prefix
  4. Contained match

Ties use plain-Arabic string length. There is no additional stable tie-breaker or locale collation.

Limits, alphabet behavior and performance

Search returns at most 100 entries; letter browsing returns at most 120. There is no pagination or separately computed full-match count. A trailing “+” means the returned count reached a cap.

Letter chips test the first normalized character of the displayed Arabic field. They do not select the source book's section, strip the definite article, or identify a word's root.

Search scans N records and sorts M matches, approximately O(N × field length + M log M). Loading and searching use the main isolate. Performance on slow mobile hardware has not been benchmarked.

06 / Data model and provenance

Read-only assets.
Traceable records.

Loading and caching

Future.wait loads the 28 asset strings. The repository decodes the documents, builds immutable entries and a normalized index, and caches both lists. Later successful loads return the cache.

An in-flight load is not deduplicated. Simultaneous initial callers can duplicate work.

Source retention

Section metadata includes source pages, extraction notes and quality counts. Original Arabic source strings and left/right columns remain in JSON even though the runtime model does not keep them.

The duplicate Dal file and older unvocalized Alif file are not bundled.

Script direction, fonts and accessibility

Arabic headwords explicitly render right-to-left. Search input chooses RTL when its current value contains a character in U+0600–U+06FF. Combined English/Arabic labels remain ordinary mixed strings.

The app bundles no text fonts and relies on platform font fallback. Myanmar in details is selectable; result meanings are capped at three lines. The UI is primarily English, and there are no localization delegates. Cross-device shaping, screen-reader use, large text and contrast still need device-level review.

07 / Verification and maintenance

Keep the repair reviewable.

Audit the corpus

The repeatable audit checks manifests, counts, IDs, Latin characters and placeholders. It separately inventories the editorial queue.

The strict editorial gate intentionally fails while unresolved source issues remain.

Test the application

Flutter tests cover normalization, bilingual search, navigation, repaired spelling, all Arabic fields and every recorded field correction.

Automated tests do not certify every translation or vowel.

Rebuild for distribution

Signed v1.0.1 APK and AAB files now contain the repaired data and selected logo. All packaged dictionary sections match the source. The old v1.0.0 files are retained separately.

The v1.0.1 release certificate matches the previous Nur APK. Physical-device testing and the editorial review queue remain outstanding.

Where to change content

Edit lib/src/config/app_content.dart for names, biographies, experience and contact details. Author/developer placeholders are still present. Contacts are copied to the clipboard; they do not automatically open external websites.

Add new section files to both pubspec.yaml and DictionaryRepository.sectionFiles, preserving their shared order. Update counts and regression expectations intentionally.

What the current architecture does not implement

No favorites, stored history, persistent settings, pronunciation audio, remote synchronization, background indexing, morphological search, database storage, online updates, CI workflow, or web/Windows/macOS runners. These are current boundaries, not promises on a roadmap.
